title: Edge cases + failure modes — Dedicated autoscaling bounds & predictive signals (working notes)
content:
Purpose
- Enumerate edge cases + failure modes for customer-configurable min/max bounds and predictive scaling mode for Dedicated.
- Define expected autoscaler behavior (deterministic, bounded) + what we emit (metrics/logs/audit) so SRE/Support can reason about it.
- These are working notes; canonical semantics should live in ADR (bounds precedence + safety invariants).

Non-negotiable invariants (repeat everywhere)
- Never exceed max bound.
- Never scale below min bound (NOTE: exception is “min cannot be met due to region capacity shortage” → we do NOT violate bounds by faking; we surface degraded state and keep retrying/backoff).
- Deterministic evaluation: for every loop we can record:
  - requested_desired (from arbitration)
  - bounded_desired (after clamp)
  - decision_reason(s) (e.g., reactive_queue_high, predictor_stale, cooldown_active, max_bound_hit)
- Backward compatibility: existing deployments keep current behavior until feature flag / explicit policy enablement.

Definitions used below (for clarity)
- min_replicas, max_replicas: customer-configured hard bounds.
- platform defaults: current autoscaler defaults (min floor, max cap) used when customer has not opted in.
- requested_desired: computed by autoscaler logic BEFORE clamp (can be influenced by reactive + predictive).
- bounded_desired: clamp(requested_desired, min_replicas, max_replicas).
- predictive mode: predictor suggests desired capacity or demand forecast; reactive signals can override predictive when predictor is wrong/unavailable. Still bounded.
- “unmet min”: bounded_desired == min_replicas but scheduler cannot provision min_replicas due to fleet shortage / quota / fragmentation.

Quick note on precedence (implementation assumption)
- If customer policy enabled:
  - bounds override platform defaults.
  - if no max is set (future?) we treat as “no customer max” but still obey hard platform safety max (internal). For now: require both min and max when enabled.
- If policy not enabled:
  - use existing platform behavior.

Edge cases / failure modes

1) Invalid config: min > max
- Symptom:
  - UI/API attempts to set min_replicas greater than max_replicas.
- Expected behavior:
  - Reject at validation time (control plane API + Console form).
  - Return explicit error message: “min_replicas must be <= max_replicas.”
  - Do not persist partial config; no rollout.
- Observability/audit:
  - Audit event: scaling_policy_update_rejected with validation_error=min_gt_max.
  - No change to effective policy.

2) Invalid config: negative values, zero, non-integer
- Symptom:
  - min=-1, max=0 (depending on whether we allow max=0), floats.
- Expected behavior:
  - Reject. For Dedicated, we should treat min>=1 as default requirement (no scale-to-zero for Dedicated).
  - If future support for scale-to-zero exists, it must be an explicit separate flag; not implied by max=0.
- Notes:
  - This is the class of bug we hit in pilot when predictor returned null and path resulted in 0 desired; guard required.

3) Config churn: rapid repeated updates (customer or automation)
- Symptom:
  - Customer scripts update bounds repeatedly (e.g., every minute) or multiple users fighting in Console.
  - Causes oscillation + audit noise; can also thrash scheduler.
- Expected behavior:
  - Rate limit updates per deployment (e.g., N updates / 10 minutes). Return 429/explicit error.
  - Autoscaler should treat policy changes as a “configuration epoch”:
    - apply immediately after propagation, but do not allow immediate scale down if it would cause a big change without observing stability window.
- Observability/audit:
  - Audit: scaling_policy_update_throttled.
  - Metric: scaling_policy_update_rate_limited_total{deployment_id,customer_id,region}.
- Operational guidance:
  - Support macro: “If you need scheduled changes, talk to Redwood; don’t do minute-level tuning.”

4) Partial propagation / stale config in autoscaler cache
- Symptom:
  - Control plane has new bounds, but autoscaler reads cached old policy for some interval.
- Expected behavior:
  - Define cache TTL + explicit invalidation on write (preferred).
  - Deterministic: autoscaler logs policy_version/policy_etag with every decision.
  - If policy cannot be fetched (control plane outage), fall back to last-known-good (LKG) for a bounded time window.
  - If LKG too old (beyond staleness threshold), enter conservative mode:
    - keep current replicas (no scale-down), allow scale-up only if reactive overload triggers (still obeying last-known max if present); if no policy known, fall back to platform defaults.
- Observability:
  - Metric: policy_fetch_errors_total, policy_staleness_seconds.
  - Alert: policy_staleness_seconds > threshold for pilot/GA deployments.

5) Migration / implicit defaults for existing deployments
- Symptom:
  - Backfill sets new fields but behavior must not change.
- Expected behavior:
  - Feature flag gate: policy_enabled=false by default.
  - Store fields but ignore until enabled.
  - UI should show “Not enabled” state and what would happen if enabled.
- Risk:
  - Any code path that treats “fields present” as “enabled” is a footgun.
- Tests:
  - Regression test: existing deployment with no policy_enabled should not clamp to 0/any unintended value.

6) Requested desired < min (scale-down pressure)
- Common causes:
  - Predictor says low demand; reactive utilization low; queue depth empty.
- Expected behavior:
  - Clamp to min. Emit bound-hit reason “min_bound_hit”.
  - Should still respect cooldown/anti-oscillation: if we are at min already, do nothing.
- Observability:
  - Counter: autoscaler_bound_hit_total{bound=min}.
  - Gauge: autoscaler_requested_desired vs autoscaler_bounded_desired.

7) Requested desired > max (scale-up pressure)
- Common causes:
  - Reactive overload, queue depth high.
  - Predictor overestimates demand.
- Expected behavior:
  - Clamp to max. Emit “max_bound_hit”.
  - If max is hit AND reactive overload persists, we must surface “bounded saturation” state.
  - Routing integration: expose bounded saturation so smart routing can degrade gracefully (fallback model/region per policy) without violating bounds.
- Alerts:
  - If max_bound_hit sustained + queue depth > threshold for X minutes → page (Dedicated SRE) + notify Support channel for customer comms.
- Customer comms guidance:
  - “You are at your configured max. To reduce queueing, either increase max or reduce workload; Redwood can help recommend.”

8) Predictor returns null / NaN / negative / out-of-range
- Symptom:
  - Forecast service bug or missing data.
- Expected behavior:
  - Treat as “prediction unavailable”; do not use value.
  - Fall back to reactive scaling only.
  - Never let null translate to 0 desired (explicit guard).
- Observability:
  - Metric: prediction_invalid_total{reason=null|nan|negative|too_large}.
  - Include predictor_version + model_id in logs for correlation.

9) Predictor stale (timestamp too old)
- Symptom:
  - Forecast pipeline lag; values are old.
- Expected behavior:
  - If forecast age > staleness threshold:
    - ignore predictive input, fall back to reactive.
    - optionally emit event “predictive_disabled_due_to_staleness”.
  - Do NOT keep using stale forecast for scale-down decisions.
- Alert:
  - prediction_staleness_seconds > threshold for pilots.

10) Predictor overestimates (false positives) → overscale
- Symptom:
  - Capacity jumps up but demand doesn’t arrive. Cost spike; possibly impacts fleet availability.
- Expected behavior:
  - Anti-oscillation: conservative step sizes for predictive-only scale-ups; require confidence threshold.
  - Use cooldowns; allow scale-down slowly and only to min.
  - If prediction error high for a rolling window, auto-disable predictive for that deployment (fail open to reactive) for a fixed backoff period.
- Observability:
  - prediction_error (MAPE / absolute error) per deployment (careful with cardinality).
  - Metric: predictive_auto_disabled_total{reason=error_high}.

11) Predictor underestimates (false negatives) → queue build before scale-up
- Symptom:
  - Daily ramp; prediction misses; reactive triggers late.
- Expected behavior:
  - Reactive signals override predictive when queue depth/saturation crosses threshold.
  - Scale-up step may be larger when overload is detected (still bounded by max).
  - If overload and max hit → bounded saturation state as above.

12) Reactive signals degraded / missing (telemetry loss)
- Symptom:
  - Missing queue depth metrics; saturation not reported; partial agent outage.
- Expected behavior:
  - Do not scale down aggressively when observability is missing.
  - If both reactive and predictive are unavailable: hold current replicas (subject to min/max clamp if config changed).
  - If only predictive available and fresh: allow limited scale-up (bounded) but keep scale-down conservative.
- Observability:
  - Metric: autoscaler_signal_missing_total{signal=queue|util|latency}.
  - Alert if signals missing for > N minutes on a deployment under pilot.

13) Region capacity shortage: cannot provision min
- Symptom:
  - Fleet lacks GPUs in region; scheduler fails placements; provisioning stalls.
- Expected behavior:
  - Autoscaler continues to request bounded_desired=min (or higher if needed) but actual stays below.
  - Expose state: unmet_min=true, unmet_reason=region_capacity_shortage (or quota, fragmentation).
  - Backoff retries to avoid thundering herd; include jitter.
  - SRE + capacity planning notified; customer notified with transparent status (Dedicated expectation).
- Must NOT do:
  - Silently reduce min.
  - Automatically shift region (out of scope; routing may degrade if configured but Dedicated isolation applies).
- Observability/alerts:
  - Gauge: autoscaler_actual_replicas.
  - Gauge: autoscaler_unmet_min (0/1).
  - Alert: unmet_min sustained > X minutes.

14) Region capacity shortage: cannot scale up to meet overload (max not hit)
- Symptom:
  - requested_desired <= max, but placement fails.
- Expected behavior:
  - Similar to unmet min; surface “unmet desired” with reason.
  - Routing may need to degrade gracefully (if allowed) but respect Dedicated constraints.

15) GPU fragmentation / wrong instance type available
- Symptom:
  - Fleet has GPUs but not the right SKU or contiguous capacity; placements fail intermittently.
- Expected behavior:
  - Treat as capacity shortage subtype (fragmentation).
  - Retry/backoff; do not oscillate requested_desired.
  - Emit reason codes to help infra planning.

16) Control plane outage during policy update
- Symptom:
  - Customer attempts to change bounds; API times out.
- Expected behavior:
  - Update either succeeds with idempotency key or fails without partial apply.
  - Autoscaler continues with LKG policy; no sudden change.
- Support guidance:
  - Ask for request_id; check audit log events.

17) Audit log pipeline lag/outage
- Symptom:
  - Compliance expects events; export to SIEM delayed.
- Expected behavior:
  - Scaling decisions must continue; audit events queued/buffered.
  - If audit pipeline down beyond threshold, create internal incident but do not block autoscaling.
- Note:
  - For enterprise accounts, we may need explicit comms if audit retention SLA is impacted.

18) Clock/timezone issues for predictive (DST, customer local time)
- Symptom:
  - Scheduled events or time-of-day model misaligned by 1 hour; spikes.
- Expected behavior:
  - Predictor interface should use UTC timestamps exclusively.
  - Console should clearly display timezone for any schedule-like input (if we add it later).
  - If predictor shows systematic offset, auto-disable predictive for that deployment until corrected.

19) Conflicting signals: reactive says scale up, predictive says scale down
- Expected behavior:
  - Arbitration rule: reactive overload wins for scale-up; predictive cannot force scale-down during overload.
  - For non-overload steady state, predictive can bias desired, but clamp + cooldown applies.
  - Always log both inputs and final reason ordering.

20) Conflicting signals: queue depth high due to downstream dependency, not capacity
- Symptom:
  - Queue depth climbs because upstream retries or downstream tool call is slow; scaling replicas won’t help.
- Expected behavior:
  - Guardrails: require corroboration signal (e.g., GPU utilization or token throughput saturation) before scaling aggressively.
  - Cap scale-up step size when only queue is high but utilization is low.
- Observability:
  - “queue_high_util_low” indicator to avoid runaway.

21) Model-level throughput changes (runtime upgrade, quantization toggles) destabilize scaling
- Symptom:
  - After rollout, each replica handles more/less load, making past forecast wrong.
- Expected behavior:
  - Predictor must incorporate recent performance (tokens/sec) or autoscaler should adjust target utilization based on measured throughput.
  - During rollout windows, reduce predictive weight or require re-learning period.
- Ops:
  - Flag in release process: any runtime/model performance change needs check of scaling behavior.

22) Cooldown and dampening corner cases
- Symptom:
  - Cooldown prevents needed scale-up (bad) or prevents needed scale-down (wastes cost).
- Expected behavior:
  - Cooldown should not block emergency scale-up when overload is severe (define threshold). It CAN block small oscillations.
  - Cooldown should block rapid scale-down after predictive overshoot.
- Logging:
  - decision_reason=cooldown_active; include time_remaining.

23) Step sizing corner cases: huge requested_desired delta
- Symptom:
  - Predictor jumps from 2 → 50 replicas.
- Expected behavior:
  - Clamp to max; also apply max_step_up per interval to avoid fleet shock.
  - Allow faster step-up if queue depth critical (still bounded), but rate limited.
- Note:
  - Fleet-level global rate limits may be needed to avoid multi-tenant thundering herd.

24) Manual operator override conflicts with bounds
- Symptom:
  - On-call tries to pin replicas for mitigation.
- Expected behavior:
  - Overrides must still respect hard bounds unless override is an explicitly privileged “break-glass” path (separately audited, time-limited).
  - If break-glass exists, it should create a loud audit event + require approval.

25) Customer sets min very high (cost + region pressure)
- Symptom:
  - min consumes too much reserved capacity; could induce region shortage.
- Expected behavior:
  - Validation warning (not block) based on platform recommended range.
  - If min cannot be met, surface unmet_min; do not auto-reduce min.
- Support guidance:
  - Encourage staged increase; coordinate with TAM/Capacity team.

26) Max too low relative to SLA target (customer-induced throttling)
- Symptom:
  - Customer hits max daily; queueing; escalations.
- Expected behavior:
  - Show max bound saturation on dashboard; provide recommended max based on observed p95 and ramp.
  - Routing can optionally degrade (customer chooses) but we will not exceed max.

27) Multi-region deployments (Dedicated in multiple regions)
- Symptom:
  - Different bounds per region; prediction may be global.
- Expected behavior:
  - Bounds evaluated per deployment per region.
  - Predictive input must be region-scoped (or explicitly split) to avoid wrong scaling.
- Out of scope note:
  - Cross-region active-active predictive placement optimization is explicitly out of scope; don’t silently rebalance.

28) Partial fleet outage / zone outage
- Symptom:
  - One AZ loses capacity; replicas reduce; scale attempts fail.
- Expected behavior:
  - Continue requesting bounded_desired, but actual may drop.
  - Surface “capacity_degraded” and unmet_min if below min.
  - Backoff to avoid repeated failed scheduling; coordinate with incident response.

29) Deployment deletion / disable while autoscaler loop running
- Symptom:
  - Deployment being torn down; autoscaler still pushing desired.
- Expected behavior:
  - Control plane should mark deployment state; autoscaler should stop acting when terminating.
  - Ensure audit logs don’t spam on termination.

30) RBAC / unauthorized updates
- Symptom:
  - Wrong user/service attempts policy update.
- Expected behavior:
  - Reject with 403; audit event includes actor + reason.
  - No state change.

31) API idempotency and retries (double writes)
- Symptom:
  - Client retries update and we apply twice (esp. if throttling).
- Expected behavior:
  - Require idempotency key for write endpoint (Console uses it).
  - Same key returns same result; audit indicates idempotent_replay=true.

32) Safety: scale-to-zero should never happen for Dedicated
- Symptom:
  - Bugs in predictor/reactive fallback cause desired=0.
- Expected behavior:
  - Enforce global floor of 1 for Dedicated deployments at the autoscaler clamp stage.
  - Unit tests: null predictor + low signals must keep at >= min (and min >= 1).

What we should always emit (minimum set)
- Metrics:
  - autoscaler_requested_replicas (gauge)
  - autoscaler_bounded_replicas (gauge)
  - autoscaler_actual_replicas (gauge)
  - autoscaler_bound_hit_total{bound=min|max} (counter)
  - autoscaler_unmet_min (gauge 0/1) + unmet_reason label (low cardinality)
  - prediction_staleness_seconds (gauge)
  - prediction_invalid_total (counter)
  - scaling_events_total{direction=up|down, reason} (counter)
- Logs (structured):
  - deployment_id, customer_id, region
  - policy_version/etag, feature_flag_state
  - inputs: reactive_summary, predictive_summary
  - requested_desired, bounded_desired, actual
  - reasons (ordered list as string)
- Audit events (compliance):
  - scaling_policy_updated (who/when/what)
  - scaling_policy_update_rejected (why)
  - scaling_decision (optional; may be sampled, but enterprise may want full retention)

Open questions / TODO
- Do we allow max to be unset (infinite) in GA? If yes, define platform hard max and how we communicate it.
- When unmet_min happens, do we page immediately or only after a delay? (Need SRE threshold + noise control.)
- How to represent “recommended range” vs hard bounds in Console without confusing customers.
- Define exact arbitration ordering and thresholds (reactive vs predictive, when we ignore predictive).

Notes from incidents/pilot (brief)
- Pilot incident: predictor returned null → unsafe downscale path (fixed via guard). Keep tests.
- Customer escalations tend to be: (a) max cap hit causing queueing; (b) min not met during shortage; (c) oscillation during ramp. These edge cases should map to dashboard panels + runbook steps.
